cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The parcel depot closes at six. Your mother's waiting outside the station. Which am I collecting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then do you want her waiting for me or waiting for her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Shall I pull over to explain, or keep driving before the depot shuts?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 restricts questions, but A5 asks another choice without maintaining specific approval over B selected priority.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 present identity causes A3 two forms of waiting; B4 parcel choice and call plan meet A5 incoming call, after an irrelevant preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains emotional stakes and B4 selects a practical division of labor, credibly trying to resolve the conflict.

heightening.evidence: B4 solution is tested by A5 mother calling A first, creating a new deadline-versus-explanation choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 six-o-clock depot closure and waiting mother establish concrete competing collections.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 pull-over choice follows B4 call plan, while A3 stock question ban is awkward.
